title: Horizontal composition of canonical additive Roos comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories with countable products [def-sp-abelian, def-weil-category-product]. For a strict tower $X$ of unbounded cochain complexes in one of them, write $\mathsf H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nX_n\to\prod_nX_n)[-1]$ in the fixed coordinates of [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Thus in degree $p+1$ the coordinates are $(\prod_nX_n^p)\oplus(\prod_nX_n^{p+1})$ and the differential is $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$. For an additive functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ (additive means preserving sums of morphisms), use $F$ also for its termwise action on complexes and towers. Let $c_{F,X}:F(\prod_n X_n)\to\prod_nF(X_n)$ be the cochain map with $n$th projection $F(\pi_n)$, and use the canonical biproduct comparison from $F(U\oplus W)$ to $F(U)\oplus F(W)$.

These comparisons give a natural cochain map
$$\kappa_{F,X}:F\mathsf H(X)\longrightarrow\mathsf H(FX)$$
whose degree-$p+1$ coordinate map is the biproduct comparison followed by $c_{F,X}^p\oplus c_{F,X}^{p+1}$. It is an isomorphism if $F$ preserves countable products. Let $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ and $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$ be additive functors and $\alpha:GF\Rightarrow L$ a natural transformation; $\alpha_X$ denotes its termwise tower map and $\alpha_{\mathsf H(X)}$ its termwise map on the Roos complex. Then
$$\mathsf H(\alpha_X)\,\kappa_{G,FX}\,G(\kappa_{F,X})
=\kappa_{L,X}\,\alpha_{\mathsf H(X)}.$$
This is equality of cochain maps with the prescribed maps on both product coordinates. For the identity functor the comparison is the identity under the canonical identifications. If a compatible family $q_n:P\to X_n$ has strict augmentation $q:P\to\mathsf H(X)$ with coordinates $(0,(q_n)_n)$, then $\kappa_{F,X}F(q)$ has coordinates $(0,(F(q_n))_n)$. No exactness or product preservation is needed for the map or its composition equation; no derived category, scalar extension or arithmetic subsequence occurs.

proof.text: Use ordinary right-to-left composition throughout. In an abelian category the biproduct projections $r_0,r_1$ and inclusions $i_0,i_1$ satisfy $r_j i_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $i_0r_0+i_1r_1=1$. Define $b_F:F(U\oplus W)\to F(U)\oplus F(W)$ by its projections $F(r_j)$. Its inverse is $a_F=F(i_0)\operatorname{pr}_0+F(i_1)\operatorname{pr}_1$: the matrix of $b_Fa_F$ has diagonal entries $1$ and off-diagonal entries $0$, and $a_Fb_F=F(i_0r_0+i_1r_1)=1$. These equations use precisely additivity and functoriality; additivity also gives $F(0)=0$ and $F(-h)=-F(h)$. Thus the canonical biproduct comparison and its coordinate rules follow directly, without any exactness assumption.

proof.text:
Put $P_X^r=\prod_n X_n^r$, with projections $\pi_n^r$, and write $d_X^r:P_X^r\to P_X^{r+1}$ for the componentwise differential. Define $c_F^r:F(P_X^r)\to P_{FX}^r$ uniquely by $\pi_n^r c_F^r=F(\pi_n^r)$. Then
$$\pi_n^{r+1}d_{FX}^r c_F^r=F(d_{X_n}^r)F(\pi_n^r)=F(\pi_n^{r+1})F(d_X^r)=\pi_n^{r+1}c_F^{r+1}F(d_X^r).$$
Hence $d_{FX}c_F=c_FF(d_X)$. For the transition $t_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n$ and $u_X=1-s_X$, the defining shift formula gives, degreewise,
$$\pi_n u_{FX}c_F=F(\pi_n)-F(t_n)F(\pi_{n+1})=F(\pi_n-t_n\pi_{n+1})=\pi_n c_FF(u_X).$$
The universal property of the product proves $u_{FX}c_F=c_FF(u_X)$. Neither calculation inverts $c_F$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, product-cone context; agent-written strict-coordinate calculation using Categories Tag 002I (definition-product) and Homology Tag 00ZY (definition-preadditive).

proof.text:
In the fixed coordinates $\mathsf H(X)^{p+1}=P_X^p\oplus P_X^{p+1}$ define $\kappa_{F,X}^{p+1}=(c_F^p\oplus c_F^{p+1})b_F$. The transported source differential is the matrix $(-F(d),-F(u_X);0,F(d))$, by step 1 and the specified differential of the strict Roos model. Consequently the first and second coordinates of $d\kappa$ are respectively $-d_{FX}c_F^p\operatorname{pr}_0-u_{FX}c_F^{p+1}\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $d_{FX}c_F^{p+1}\operatorname{pr}_1$. Step 2 rewrites them as $-c_F^{p+1}F(d_X^p)\operatorname{pr}_0-c_F^{p+1}F(u_X^{p+1})\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $c_F^{p+2}F(d_X^{p+1})\operatorname{pr}_1$, the coordinates of $\kappa F(d)$. Thus these maps form a cochain map. Write $e_{j,n,X}^{p+1}=\pi_n^{p+j}r_j$ for $j=0,1$. Its defining, unique coordinate rule is
$$e_{j,n,FX}^{p+1}\kappa_{F,X}^{p+1}=F(e_{j,n,X}^{p+1}).$$
Uniqueness follows by first the two biproduct projections and then all product projections.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, product-cone context; agent-written strict-coordinate calculation using Categories Tag 002I (definition-product) and Homology Tag 00ZY (definition-preadditive).

proof.text: For a strict tower cochain map $h:X\to Y$, the strict Roos map is diagonal on the two product coordinates. Therefore $e_{j,n,Y}\mathsf H(h)=h_n^{p+j}e_{j,n,X}$. After $e_{j,n,FY}$, the two sides of $\mathsf H(Fh)\kappa_{F,X}=\kappa_{F,Y}F(\mathsf H(h))$ become respectively $F(h_n^{p+j})F(e_{j,n,X})$ and $F(e_{j,n,Y}\mathsf H(h))$, which agree by functoriality. The coordinate uniqueness of step 3 proves naturality of $\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, product-cone context; agent-written strict-coordinate calculation using Categories Tag 002I (definition-product) and Homology Tag 00ZY (definition-preadditive).

proof.text:
Naturality of $\alpha:GF\Rightarrow L$ with respect to each differential and transition makes its termwise maps a strict tower cochain map $\alpha_X$ and a cochain map $\alpha_{\mathsf H(X)}$. In degree $p+1$, compose the asserted horizontal equation with $e_{j,n,LX}$, for each $j=0,1$ and $n$. The left side becomes
$$\alpha_{X_n^{p+j}}\,e_{j,n,GFX}\kappa_{G,FX}G(\kappa_{F,X})=\alpha_{X_n^{p+j}}\,G(e_{j,n,FX})G(\kappa_{F,X})=\alpha_{X_n^{p+j}}\,GF(e_{j,n,X}).$$
The right side becomes $L(e_{j,n,X})\alpha_{\mathsf H(X)^{p+1}}$. These are equal by naturality of $\alpha$ for the single morphism $e_{j,n,X}:\mathsf H(X)^{p+1}\to X_n^{p+j}$. Coordinate uniqueness proves the displayed equality as actual cochain maps. It uses neither invertibility of $\alpha$ nor preservation of products.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, product-cone context; agent-written strict-coordinate calculation using Categories Tag 002I (definition-product) and Homology Tag 00ZY (definition-preadditive).

proof.text: If $F$ preserves countable products, the cone with vertex $F(P_X^r)$ and projections $F(\pi_n^r)$ is itself a product cone. Its universal property gives $v^r:P_{FX}^r\to F(P_X^r)$ with $F(\pi_n^r)v^r=\pi_n^r$. The projection equations give $c_F^rv^r=1$ and $v^rc_F^r=1$, by uniqueness for the two product cones. Together with step 1 this makes each $\kappa^{p+1}$ invertible, with inverse $a_F((c_F^p)^{-1}\oplus(c_F^{p+1})^{-1})$. Multiplying $d\kappa=\kappa F(d)$ on the two sides by these inverses shows that the inverses commute with differentials, so $\kappa$ is a cochain isomorphism. For $F=\mathrm{id}$, the coordinate rule in step 3 is $e_{j,n,X}\kappa=e_{j,n,X}$; coordinate uniqueness gives $\kappa_{\mathrm{id},X}=1$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, product-cone context; agent-written strict-coordinate calculation using Categories Tag 002I (definition-product) and Homology Tag 00ZY (definition-preadditive).

proof.text:
Let $q:P\to\mathsf H(X)$ be the stated augmentation. Its shifted coordinates are $e_{0,n,X}q=0$ and its unshifted coordinates are $e_{1,n,X}q=q_n^{p+1}$. Step 3 gives
$$e_{0,n,FX}\kappa_{F,X}F(q)=F(0)=0,\qquad e_{1,n,FX}\kappa_{F,X}F(q)=F(q_n^{p+1}).$$
These are exactly the coordinates $(0,(F(q_n))_n)$, since product projections determine each coordinate. The family remains compatible because $F(t_n)F(q_{n+1})=F(t_nq_{n+1})=F(q_n)$. This proves augmentation compatibility for the same specified map.
